# nullplatform_workflow_alias (Resource)

Publishes a revision of a workflow under a name (an alias, such as `live`) and, while `active`, keeps it activated: activation registers the revision's triggers (webhooks, schedules, and the notification channels of the platform's triggers, such as a checklist item's). Point `revision` at `nullplatform_workflow.<name>.revision` and every change of the definition is published in the same apply. The resource `id` is `<workflow_id>/<name>`.

~> **Note:** Activation and deactivation act as the identity of the provider's API key: it creates and deletes the notification channels of channel triggers, so it must be allowed to manage notification channels at each such trigger's NRN. Moving to a new revision is not atomic: the alias moves, then activates; if that activation fails, the API leaves the alias inactive, the apply fails, and the next apply activates it again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    nullplatform = {
      source = "nullplatform/nullplatform"
    }
  }
}

provider "nullplatform" {}

variable "checklist_nrn" {
  type        = string
  description = "The NRN whose checklist items start the workflow."
  default     = "organization=1:account=2"
}

resource "nullplatform_workflow" "release_notify" {
  name = "release-notify"
  key  = "release-notify"

  definition = jsonencode({
    steps = {
      start = {
        id         = "start"
        name       = "On release"
        pluginType = "webhook"
        config     = { path = "/release", mode = "start" }
      }
      announce = {
        id         = "announce"
        name       = "Announce"
        pluginType = "log"
        config     = { message = "A release was announced" }
      }
    }
    connections = [{ id = "c1", from = "start", to = "announce" }]
  })
}

# The alias follows the workflow's latest revision: every change of the
# definition is published and activated in the same apply.
resource "nullplatform_workflow_alias" "live" {
  workflow_id = nullplatform_workflow.release_notify.id
  name        = "live"
  revision    = nullplatform_workflow.release_notify.revision
}

# The URL ends in a token that is the capability to start the workflow, so it
# is sensitive. It is keyed by trigger id.
output "release_notify_webhook_url" {
  value     = nullplatform_workflow_alias.live.webhook_urls["start"]
  sensitive = true
}

# A workflow started by a checklist item: activating its alias registers the
# notification channel of the trigger at the NRN it names.
resource "nullplatform_workflow" "payments_gate" {
  name = "payments-gate"

  definition = jsonencode({
    steps = {
      gate = {
        id         = "gate"
        name       = "On checklist"
        pluginType = "np-checklist-trigger"
        config = {
          kind       = "payments-gate"
          nrn        = var.checklist_nrn
          mode       = "start"
          pathPrefix = "/np/checklist/payments-gate"
        }
      }
      say = {
        id         = "say"
        name       = "Say"
        pluginType = "log"
        config     = { message = "dispatched" }
      }
    }
    connections = [{ id = "c1", from = "gate", to = "say", sourcePort = "default", targetPort = "default" }]
  })
}

resource "nullplatform_workflow_alias" "payments_gate_live" {
  workflow_id = nullplatform_workflow.payments_gate.id
  name        = "live"
  revision    = nullplatform_workflow.payments_gate.revision
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The alias's name, such as `live`. `latest` is the API's own and cannot be managed. Changing it replaces the alias: the old one is deactivated and deleted, the new one created and activated.
- `revision` (Number) The revision the alias publishes, usually `nullplatform_workflow.<name>.revision`. While `active`, changing it moves the alias and activates it again, which registers the triggers of the new revision and releases the ones it no longer has.
- `workflow_id` (String) The id of the workflow, usually `nullplatform_workflow.<name>.id`: its id, not its key. Changing it replaces the alias.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the alias is activated: its triggers registered and listening. Defaults to `true`. With `false` the alias is published but nothing triggers it; setting it deactivates the alias. An alias deactivated outside Terraform shows in the plan, and the next apply activates it again.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `webhook_urls` (Map of String, Sensitive) The URL of each trigger of the published revision that the engine serves over HTTP (a `webhook` trigger, and the ones the platform's notifications reach), by trigger id, while the alias is active; empty while it is not. Sensitive: the URL ends in a token that is the capability to start the workflow.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# An alias is imported by "<workflow id or key>/<alias>". The state keeps the workflow's id.
terraform import nullplatform_workflow_alias.live release-notify/live
terraform import nullplatform_workflow_alias.live wf_0123456789abcdef/live
```
